source.text: tantrasāra, saptamam āhnikam tatra samasta eva ayaṃ mūrtivaicitryābhāsanaśaktijo deśādhvā saṃvidi viśrāntaḥ taddvāreṇa śūnye buddhau prāṇe nāḍīcakrānucakreṣu bahiḥ śarīre yāval liṅgasthaṇḍilapratimādau samasto 'dhvā pariniṣṭhitaḥ taṃ samastam adhvānaṃ dehe vilāpya dehaṃ ca prāṇe taṃ dhiyi tāṃ śūnye tatsaṃvedane nirbharaparipūrṇasaṃvit sampadyate ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasvarūpajñaḥ taduttīrṇāṃ saṃvidaṃ paramaśivarūpāṃ paśyan viśvamayīm api saṃvedayeta aparathā vedyabhāgam eva kaṃcit paratvena gṛhṇīyān māyāgarbhādhikāriṇaṃ viṣṇubrahmādikaṃ vā tasmād avaśyaṃ prakriyājñānapareṇa bhavitavyam // abhts_7.1 tad uktaṃ na prakriyāparaṃ jñānam iti // abhts_7.2 tatra pṛthivītattvaṃ śatakoṭipravistīrṇaṃ brahmāṇḍagolakarūpam // abhts_7.3 tasya antaḥ kālāgnir narakāḥ pātālāni pṛthivī svargo yāvad brahmaloka iti // abhts_7.4 brahmāṇḍabāhye rudrāṇāṃ śatam // abhts_7.5 na ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ saṃkhyā vidyate // abhts_7.6 tato dharātattvād daśaguṇaṃ jalatattvam // abhts_7.7 tata uttarottaraṃ daśaguṇam ahaṃkārāntam // abhts_7.8 tad yathā jalaṃ tejo vāyur nabhaḥ tanmātrapañcakākṣaikādaśagarbho 'haṃkāraś ceti // abhts_7.9 ahaṃkārāt śataguṇaṃ buddhitattvam // abhts_7.10 tataḥ sahasradhā prakṛtitattvam etāvat prakṛtyaṇḍam // abhts_7.11 tac ca brahmāṇḍavad asaṃkhyam // abhts_7.12 prakṛtitattvāt puruṣatattvaṃ ca daśasahasradhā // abhts_7.13 puruṣān niyatiḥ lakṣadhā // abhts_7.14 niyater uttarottaraṃ daśalakṣadhā kalātattvāntam // abhts_7.15 tad yathā niyatiḥ rāgo 'śuddhavidyā kālaḥ kalā ceti // abhts_7.16 kalātattvāt koṭidhā māyā etāvat māyāṇḍam // abhts_7.17 māyātattvāt śuddhavidyā daśakoṭiguṇitā // abhts_7.18 vidyātattvād īśvaratattvaṃ śatakoṭidhā // abhts_7.19 īśvaratattvāt sādākhyaṃ sahasrakoṭidhā // abhts_7.20 sādākhyāt vṛndaguṇitaṃ śaktitattvam iti śaktyaṇḍam // abhts_7.21 sā śaktir vyāpya yato viśvam adhvānam antarbahir āste tasmād vyāpinī // abhts_7.22 evam etāni uttarottaram āvaraṇatayā vartamānāni tattvāny uttaraṃ vyāpakaṃ pūrvaṃ vyāpyam iti sthityā vartante // abhts_7.23 yāvad aśeṣaśaktitattvānto 'dhvā śivatattvena vyāptaḥ // abhts_7.24 śivatattvaṃ punar aparimeyaṃ sarvādhvottīrṇaṃ sarvādhvavyāpakaṃ ca // abhts_7.25 etat tattvāntarālavartīni yāni bhuvanāni tatpataya eva atra pṛthivyāṃ sthitā iti // abhts_7.26 teṣv āyataneṣu ye mriyante teṣāṃ tatra tatra gatiṃ te vitaranti // abhts_7.27 kramāc ca ūrdhvordhvaṃ prerayanti dīkṣākrameṇa // abhts_7.28

l1_text:
## tsa07-p01
Therein, entire itself, born of form-variety-manifesting-power, is the place-course, resting in consciousness. Through its door, in void, in intellect, in breath, in channel-wheel-subwheels, outside, in body, down to liṅga-altar-image and the rest, the whole course is completed. Having dissolved that whole course in body, and body in breath, and that in mind, and that in void — in that consciousness, brimming-full consciousness results. Knowing thirty-six-principle-nature, seeing consciousness beyond that as supreme-Śiva-natured, one should sense it as universe-made too. Otherwise one would grasp some knowable portion alone as other — Māyā-womb-officer, or Viṣṇu-Brahmā-and-the-rest. Hence one must necessarily be devoted to process-knowledge. (7.1) As stated: "No knowledge beyond process." (7.2) Therein earth-principle, hundred-crore-spread, universe-egg-globe-formed. (7.3) Inside it: time-fire, hells, underworlds, earth, heaven, up to Brahmā-world. (7.4) Outside the universe-egg, a hundred of Rudras. (7.5) Nor is number of universe-eggs found. (7.6) Than earth-principle, tenfold water-principle. (7.7) Then successively tenfold up to ego. (7.8) Namely: water, fire, wind, void, five-subtle-five-sense-eleven-wombed ego. (7.9) Than ego, hundredfold intellect-principle. (7.10) Thence thousandfold nature-principle — so far nature-egg. (7.11) And it, like universe-egg, countless. (7.12) Than nature-principle, ten-thousandfold person-principle. (7.13) Than person, hundred-thousandfold destiny. (7.14) Than destiny, successively ten-lakh-fold up to art-principle. (7.15) Namely: destiny, passion, impure knowledge, time, and art. (7.16) Than art-principle, crore-fold Māyā — so far Māyā-egg. (7.17) Than Māyā-principle, ten-crore-multiplied pure knowledge. (7.18) Than knowledge-principle, hundred-crore-fold Lord-principle. (7.19) Than Lord-principle, thousand-crore-fold High-tongued. (7.20) Than High-tongued, crowd-multiplied power-principle — thus power-egg. (7.21) That power, pervading — since the universe-course inside-outside abides — hence pervader. (7.22) Thus these, successively as coverings proceeding, are principles; the latter is pervader, the former pervaded — thus situated they proceed. (7.23) Until the course to power-principle-end is pervaded by Śiva-principle. (7.24) Śiva-principle is immeasurable, beyond-all-courses and pervading-all-courses. (7.25) Such are worlds standing between principles — their lords alone here on earth stand. (7.26) In those shrines, who die, to them there and there movement they grant. (7.27) And in order up and up they impel, by initiation-course. (7.28)
l2_text:
## tsa07-p01 — how big the world is
The place-course is one thing born of power showing every shape, and it rests in awareness. Through its gate the whole course gets finished — in the void, in mind, in breath, in wheels within wheels of channels, outside, in the body, down to the liṅga on the altar and the temple image. Melt the course into the body, the body into breath, breath into mind, mind into the void — and what knows all that brims over as full awareness. Know the thirty-six this way, and see the awareness past them as supreme Śiva — yet still taste it as the universe too. Else you'll grab some one knowable as "other" — some Māyā officer, some Viṣṇu — so learn the process, no shortcuts: "no knowing past process." Earth spreads a hundred crores wide, an egg-globe of a universe — fire of time, hells, underworlds, earth, heaven to Brahmā's world inside; a hundred Rudras outside; eggs past counting. Water, ten times earth; then ten times at every step to ego (water, fire, wind, void, five subtles, eleven senses in ego's womb); mind a hundred times ego; nature a thousand — the nature-egg, countless like the world-egg; person ten thousand times nature; destiny a hundred thousand; then ten lakhs at a step to art (destiny, passion, half-knowing, time, art); Māyā a crore past art — the Māyā-egg; pure knowing ten crores past Māyā; the Lord a hundred crores past knowing; the High-voiced a thousand crores past the Lord; power past him by crowds — the power-egg, called Pervader because the world's course sits inside and outside her. Each later principle wears the earlier as its cover, pervading it; and Śiva pervades up to power's end — himself past measure, past every course and through them. Between the principles stand worlds, whose lords are posted here on earth: die in their shrines and they ferry you onward and upward, by initiation's road.

Between the principles stand worlds, whose lords are posted here on earth: die in their shrines and they ferry you onward and upward, by initiation's road.

The passage moves in four steps. (1) Place-course = form-variety-manifesting-power, resting in consciousness; through it the whole course completes in void/intellect/breath/channels/body/liṅga-altar-image; dissolve the course back into void → brimming consciousness. (2) Knowing 36 natures, seeing beyond-consciousness as supreme Śiva yet universe-made (else grasping some knowable or Māyā-officer/Viṣṇu as other) → process-knowledge mandatory. (3) Magnitude ladder: earth (100-crore) → water 10× → … → ego (5+5+11) → intellect 100× → nature 1000× (= nature-egg, countless) → person 10,000× → destiny 100,000× → art (10-lakh steps) → Māyā crore (= Māyā-egg) → pure knowledge 10-crore → Lord 100-crore → High-tongued 1000-crore → power crowd-multiplied (= power-egg, pervader). (4) Layering (latter pervades former as coverings; Śiva pervades up to power's end) + shrine mechanics (worlds between principles; dying in shrines grants transits; impel upward by initiation).

c1.function: Establishes the deśādhvā (place-course) and the 36-principle magnitude ladder; process-knowledge enjoined.
c1.local_context: A06 (sthāna/kāla) precedes; A07 teaches place-course; A08 (kārya-kāraṇa) follows.
c1.boundary: Purāṇic interiors (kālāgni, narakas, pātālas) external. Shrine mechanics (dīkṣākrameṇa) external. Magnitude ladder is Abhinava's own scaling.
